stock.opening: GM's weighted path reaches $117.00 in October 2029, after $82.23 in October 2027. It hinges on vehicle pricing and cash generation enduring.
stock.closing: The full GM memo also answers how GM’s business works, how it compares with rivals, what management is doing, and which risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could GM's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted path is modestly positive, but the possible outcomes remain wide. The weighted price is $82.23 in October 2027, a 1% total return including dividends. It reaches $98.00 in October 2028, a 21% return. By October 2029, it reaches $117.00, a 45% return.
At that last date, the bear case gives $71.86 and the bull case gives $197.05. Today’s price is $82.25. The bear receives 35% probability. The base receives 50%, while the bull receives 15%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right—or wrong—for GM?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires weaker affordability, heavier discounts and lower production, so fixed costs are absorbed over fewer vehicles. EV charges, settlements and higher GM Financial losses then constrain cash and buybacks. It leads to $56.62 in October 2027 and $71.86 in October 2029. Its 35% probability exceeds the specialists’ 30% bear view because these risks could reinforce one another.

The bull case requires successful Silverado and Sierra launches, durable pricing, better factory utilization, faster warranty and EV savings, and growing software renewals. It leads to $114.33 in October 2027 and $197.05 in October 2029. Its probability is 15% because the measured-profit path reaches its highest level only if several uncertain improvements persist through 2029.

paragraphs.text: Dividends make a simpler claim on cash because they pay shareholders directly. GM’s latest quarterly rate of $0.18 implies $0.72 a year if maintained. earnings.title: GM earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: GM reports on October 20, 2026, with guidance, recent results and key costs to watch.
earnings.opening: GM's next results are expected on October 20, 2026. Watch whether third-quarter costs fit management’s timing and later commodity benefits remain credible.
earnings.closing: The full GM memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: GM makes Chevrolet, GMC, Buick and Cadillac vehicles. For 2026, it guides to **$14,000–$16,000 million of EBIT-adjusted**, meaning operating earnings before interest and taxes after selected special items are removed, and **$12.00–$14.00 of adjusted earnings per diluted share**.

Reported profit is lower because it includes every recognized gain and loss. If a factory bought for $1 billion is now worth only $600 million, GM records a $400 million impairment. That reduces reported profit and the factory’s recorded value, even though the initial entry may not require immediate cash. GM’s reported net-income guidance is **$8,400–$9,800 million**, so adjusted earnings and shareholder profit answer different questions.

blocks.heading: Did GM keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: GM’s technology record is less consistent. It abandoned its earlier target to produce 400,000 electric vehicles through the first half of 2024 and stopped funding Cruise’s robotaxi expansion. By the July 2026 results call, EV-related charges since the second half of 2025 had reached US$10.9 billion. Anderson’s one-time US$24 million award creates a clear accountability test: GM now expects better integrated products and execution.

blocks.heading: What do GM's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose from $47,122 million to $48,026 million, but net income fell from $1,895 million to $1,305 million. The comparison with the same quarter a year earlier is more useful than a sequential comparison because late 2025 included a large operating loss.

blocks.heading: What should GM watch on October 20, 2026?

paragraphs.text: The nearest test is GM’s **October 20, 2026** results. Costs do not always reach reported vehicle costs immediately: parts may sit in inventory or pass through suppliers first. The release should show whether third-quarter costs fit management’s timing and whether later commodity benefits remain credible.
